text:
support_tina: hi @eng-sre — customer hitting intermittent 503s. They provided a request id I can barely read in the headers, hoping we can pull server-side logs. Claim: request_id=req_20260315_abc123_def456, happened around 2026-03-15T14:22:03Z UTC. Org: org-zen123. Customer grabbed a quick curl and got 503. Can we look this up?

jamie: can you paste the exact request_id (looks truncated). also which env/region? hosted prod? note: hosted retention is 14d by default, so if this is older we might be out of hot logs.

support_tina: full id pasted from their header: req_20260315_abc123_def456. region: prod-us-east-1. they also sent response headers: 
  X-Request-ID: req_20260315_abc123_def456
  Status: 503
  Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 14:22:03 GMT

  sanitized curl they ran:
  ```
  curl -i -X POST \"https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate\" \\   -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \\   -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\   -d '{"input":"..."}' \\
  ```

alex_m: running a quick search. use this Kibana/KQL to try locally:
  request_id.keyword:\ \"req_20260315_abc123_def456\" OR trace.id:\ \"req_20260315_abc123_def456\"
  if you have ES access, equivalent DSL: { \"query\": { \"term\": { \"request_id\": \"req_20260315_abc123_def456\" }}}
  querying prod-cluster now.

logs-bot: Started search for req_20260315_abc123_def456 in prod-cluster-1 (index patterns: logs-*, shards: 12).

alex_m: quick update — search returned no hits in hot indices. Based on the timestamp the event is outside the 14-day retention window for hosted prod. Last indexed event for that org in prod is 2026-03-23, so 2026-03-15 is past TTL.

alex_m: we have two options: 1) request a cold retrieval from the log archive (if available) — needs infra approval and ~48-72h turnaround, or 2) ask the customer for a repro + debug bundle (client logs + full sanitized payload + response headers) so we can reproduce live and capture new logs.

infra-luke: I can open a retrieval ticket. I'll need: request_id(s), exact UTC time window (start/end), org id, and a short business justification. I'll file INC-7891 for this retrieval and coordinate with SRE-oncall. ETA 48-72h once approved. Note: archive retrieval may incur egress/storage charges for enterprise contracts.

infra-luke: sample payload for customer repro — ask them to include --dump-header and a custom X-Request-ID so we can correlate if it happens again:
  ```
  curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \\  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\  -H 'X-Request-ID: customer-probe-<timestamp>' \\  -d @payload.json \\  --dump-header headers.txt \\
  ```

jamie: also ask them to attach a debug bundle from their client/service (if they have one) and include timestamps in ISO8601. If they can't reproduce live, the archive request is the only route.

support_tina: copying the steps to the customer now and requesting the following: full curl + payload.json + headers.txt + exact ISO timestamps + screenshot of X-Request-ID in their client logs. I'll also open a support ticket linking INC-7891 once infra-luke creates it. Thanks all :pray:

jamie: minor note — for future we can suggest they set a custom X-Request-ID header themselves in the client to make hunts faster. Also include the region, account id, and route path.

support_tina: acknowledged — updating the customer and closing the loop here until we hear back or infra posts INC-7891.
